_comment: Human-verified Booklet B question start positions, applied by
build/index_questions.py. This is section 1.6.1's mcq-positions.json
precedent (Booklet A) carried over to Booklet B, for the same reason: both
automatic readers can land on the same wrong answer at once, or on none at
all, and when that happens a question's sub-parts are silently absorbed by
whichever neighbour DID get recognised -- the most dangerous failure this
pipeline has (CLAUDE.md section 1.6).
2026-prelim-aitong needed five corrections, four different failure shapes
in one paper:
* Q34 (p4): tesseract garbled '34.' into an unrelated three-letter word
('sit.') and Vision did no better, so nothing recovered it at all and p4
(plus p5, its own overflow page) were silently folded into Q33 (whose
span became p3-5). Q34 turns out to run two thematically-related
mini-scenarios under one number -- paper P/Q/R's fall time on p4, then
animal X's gliding skin on p5 -- both about how surface area affects
air resistance, which is why the mismatch in subject matter between the
two pages is real and not a sign the pages are out of order.
* Q32 (p2): both readers misread '32.' -- tesseract dropped it to nothing,
Vision read '82.', which is out of the paper's stated Q31-Q41 range and
so never became a candidate at all. Nothing recovers a number neither
reader ever proposed; p2 was silently folded into Q31.
* Q36 (p8): tesseract dropped it to nothing; Vision read '34.', which IS
in range and did become a candidate -- but 34 sits, by page order, after
the genuine Q35 (p6) and before the genuine Q37 (p10), so the longest-run
chooser had to pick one of '...,35,37,...' or '...,34,37,...' and correctly
dropped the phantom 34 rather than the real 35. That left p8 an orphan,
silently folded into Q35 (whose span became p6-9, four pages for what is
really two two-page questions on unrelated scenarios -- community/pond,
then Kaili's coffee).
* Q38 (p12) / Q39 (p13): tesseract read BOTH correctly ('38.' at p12, '39.'
at p13) -- the one case in this paper where the base reader had no
trouble. Vision misread p12's '38.' as '39.', and because 'where both
readers named the same line, Vision's number wins' (index_questions.py's
own stated policy, correct in every other case in this corpus), Vision's
wrong 39 overwrote tesseract's right 38 at p12. p13's own correct
tesseract '39' then lost the resulting tie to the wrong-but-earlier p12
'39', leaving Q38 absent entirely and Q39's span stretched across both
pages -- Sam's sand-pit question and Paul's rice-cooker question filed
under one label.
All four were confirmed by reading the actual page image directly (not the
OCR text) and checking each page's own footer -- 'Question N continues on
the next page' / 'B-<n>' -- against its question paper cover page. This
file is committed on purpose: work-b/ is regenerated, so a verified reading
recorded only there would be lost on the next rebuild. Keys are paper id,
then question number, then the page it starts on.
